name: home Wi-Fi hubs
label: Home Wi-Fi equipment

modes.title: Hubs restarting by themselves
modes.symptom: hubs restarting by themselves several times an hour
customer_says: My hub keeps switching itself off and on again. Every time it does, the whole house loses Wi-Fi.
The Wi-Fi box restarts on its own. The lights go out, come back, and ten minutes later it does it again.
Our hub is stuck in a loop of rebooting. I haven't touched it and it just keeps restarting.
The hub won't stay up. It runs for a little while and then all the lights go off and it starts again.

causes.cause: a faulty firmware release pushed to the hubs overnight
fixes: rolling the hubs back to the previous firmware release

causes.cause: a memory leak in the hub's parental control module
fixes: pushing a patched parental control module to the hubs

causes.cause: a bad configuration file sent by the remote management server
fixes: resending a corrected configuration file to every affected hub

workarounds: plug one computer straight into the hub with a network cable
leave the hub alone between restarts rather than switching it off at the wall
aftercare: leave the hub powered on overnight so it can finish updating
reconnect any device that has not rejoined the Wi-Fi by itself

modes.title: Wi-Fi network not visible
modes.symptom: hubs no longer broadcasting their Wi-Fi network name
customer_says: My Wi-Fi network has vanished. The hub is on, but none of my devices can see it in the list.
The Wi-Fi name isn't showing up any more on my phone or my laptop, even though the hub's lights look normal.
I can't find our Wi-Fi at all. It is as if the hub has stopped sending out a signal.
The hub is powered on, but the wireless has disappeared. A cable works, the Wi-Fi doesn't.

causes.cause: a radio driver fault triggered by a channel plan change
fixes: restoring the previous channel plan on the hubs

causes.cause: a wrongly enabled wireless schedule in the hub settings
fixes: clearing the wireless schedule on the affected hubs

causes.cause: a regulatory database update that disabled both radio bands
fixes: reissuing the regulatory database to the hubs

workarounds: connect essential devices to the hub by network cable
press the WPS button for five seconds to wake the wireless radios
aftercare: forget the Wi-Fi network on a device and join it again if it will not reconnect
check that the Wi-Fi light on the hub is steady white

modes.title: Wi-Fi extenders offline
modes.symptom: Wi-Fi extenders losing their link to the hub
customer_says: The Wi-Fi boosters upstairs have stopped working. They show a red light and the bedrooms have no signal.
My extender pods have all gone offline. Wi-Fi is fine next to the hub, but dead everywhere else.
The little booster units won't connect to the hub any more, so half the house has no Wi-Fi.
Our Wi-Fi extenders keep flashing red. They used to work fine and I haven't moved them.

causes.cause: a mesh pairing bug in the latest extender software
an expired pairing key on the mesh controller
fixes: renewing the pairing key on the mesh controller

causes.cause: a clash between the extender channel and a new hub setting
fixes: moving the extenders onto a clear channel remotely

workarounds: move an extender into the same room as the hub until it pairs again
join devices to the hub's own Wi-Fi name instead of the extender's
aftercare: put each extender back in its usual room once its light turns white
restart any extender that still shows a red light

modes.title: Devices refused by the hub
modes.symptom: hubs rejecting devices with a wrong password message
customer_says: My hub says the Wi-Fi password is wrong, and I know it isn't. Nothing new will connect.
Every device gets a wrong password error on our Wi-Fi. It is the same password we've always used.
The Wi-Fi keeps asking for the password and then refusing it. I've typed it in a dozen times.
None of our gadgets can join the Wi-Fi. They all say the password is incorrect, even though it's printed on the hub.

causes.cause: a security setting changed to a mode older devices cannot use
fixes: putting the hubs back into mixed security mode

causes.cause: a corrupted password store after an interrupted hub update
fixes: rebuilding the password store on each affected hub

causes.cause: a fault in the device approval list on the hubs
fixes: resetting the device approval list remotely

workarounds: use the guest network printed on the card under the hub
connect by network cable while the wireless sign-in is being repaired
aftercare: join the main Wi-Fi again with the password on the hub's label
remove the guest network from devices that used it

wrong_customer_side: a hub placed too close to a microwave oven
a power adapter that does not belong to the hub
too many devices connected in the household
a hub that has overheated inside a cupboard
wrong_provider_side: a recall of an older hub model
a line fault at the local exchange
a scheduled security scan of customer equipment
interference from a new mobile mast in the area
